subject.title: [Feature]: expose promptMode parameter in sessions_spawn for deterministic blank sub-agents

question: Should model-callable `sessions_spawn` expose `promptMode`, including `promptMode="none"`, and what runtime/tool safety constraints should apply if it does?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the choice changes public tool API surface and the child agent's prompt safety/context envelope, which automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve constrained native promptMode
options.body: Expose `promptMode` only for native sub-agent runs with current defaults preserved, explicit docs, and tests proving task, attachments, sandbox, and tool-policy behavior under `none`.

options.title: Keep promptMode trusted-only
options.body: Leave `promptMode` off `sessions_spawn` and document that blank/raw runs require trusted lower-level runtime callers or a future maintainer-owned surface.

options.title: Design a semantic blank-worker mode
options.body: Add a higher-level isolated-worker option instead of exposing the raw prompt enum, trading a larger design step for a narrower public safety contract.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained native promptMode
recommendation.body: Expose `promptMode` only for native sub-agent runs with current defaults preserved, explicit docs, and tests proving task, attachments, sandbox, and tool-policy behavior under `none`.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced `sessions_spawn` and has the strongest feature-history signal across spawn and prompt-mode surfaces.
